page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on KVM hypervisors and powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The server features 16 physical x86_64 cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs. Memory is provisioned at 64 GB, yielding a vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1:2 (2.0 GB per vCPU). Hardware capabilities include 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and instruction set support for AVX-512, AES, BMI2, and FMA. Baseline network throughput is configured at 10 Gbps, and no local disk storage is bundled with the instance.

Performance evaluation shows a distinct contrast between single-threaded efficiency and parallel multi-core scaling. Single-core tests such as Geekbench single-core (958.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (19.13 GB/sec) rank in weaker percentile brackets. Conversely, multi-core metrics scale effectively across all 32 vCPUs, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 23029.39, a multi-core stress-ng score of 23532.01, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reaching 104.04 GB/sec. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 98.09 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput records 14.01 GB/sec.

The resource profile of the ecs.c5.8xlarge instance favors workloads prioritizing parallel vCPU capacity over per-core clock speed or large memory footprints. Without local storage drives, storage-dependent applications rely on external block storage. The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU allocation delivers cost-efficient resource density for parallel tasks, including software compilation, batch processing, static web traffic, microservices, and general compute-heavy execution.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 16 physical cores supporting hyperthreading for 32 vCPUs, it provides 64 GB of system memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio typical of compute-heavy configurations. The instance includes 33 MB of L3 cache, supports AVX-512 extension instructions, operates under KVM hypervisors, and provides a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. It lacks bundled local disk storage, relying entirely on remote storage volumes. While single-core synthetic benchmarks place per-thread performance in lower tiers, multi-core evaluation metrics highlight steady average throughput across parallel CPU tasks, static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression. The hardware profile offers reliable execution density for compute-bound parallel workloads, microservices, and distributed web applications that benefit from dedicated vCPU allocation without requiring heavy per-core memory capacity.
